ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an arrow-pushing mechanism structure, with the main body being a fused indolinone/lactam skeleton, a benzene ring at the lower left, and a lactam carbonyl with NH at the bottom; the upper left is connected to an amine side chain containing two Boc protecting groups. The upper-right reaction fragment shows a carbonyl/enol ether region containing OMe and a negatively charged oxygen, with multiple curved arrows nearby; wedge/dashed stereochemistry and a rightward H are also marked in the structure. Reasoning: Only change the upper-right conjugated fragment involved by the curved arrows, while keeping the benzene ring, fused lactam skeleton, two Boc groups, and the indicated stereocenter unchanged. The lone pair of the negative oxygen pushes back to form a carbonyl-type bond, the π electrons move along the conjugated ring segment, and according to the arrows the methoxy group leaves/is neutralized. The main product molecule therefore forms the upper conjugated enol-dicarbonyl fragment, i.e. O=C1C(O)=C..., while retaining the lower lactam carbonyl and the Boc-protected amine side chain. Written as SMILES according to this connectivity and stereochemistry: O=C1C(O)=C[C@]2([H])C(Nc3c([C@@]21CCN(C(OC(C)(C)C)=O)C(OC(C)(C)C)=O)cccc3)=O.
